tasks.short: Schedule client appointments by phone, chat or the book.

steps.what: Take the client appointment request by phone or chat
Find a free slot on the salon agenda
Agree the service and time with the client
Schedule that appointment on the salon agenda
Send a reminder of the stored appointment

tasks.design: The {OTHER} salon agenda publishes her bookable hours and each stored service duration, and the client writes a standard appointment into a free slot. She still hears and agrees first visits, colour corrections and parties, at the same length as today, and she types only those. A reminder is sent only from a booking that already has a phone number, a service and a start time; a missing phone means no reminder and no chase.
tasks.previous_blocker: Free slots sat on the salon screen or a paper page, so a client could take a time only by phone, chat or at the desk.
tasks.enabler_now: The agenda can offer only slots that fit a stored duration and her published hours, and it can message the phone number already stored on the booking.
tasks.still_hard: A first visit, a colour correction and a party still need a talk about length and who is free.
tasks.human_edge: She sets the hours and the durations the page may sell, and she can refuse a request that does not fit a published service.

ambition.what: Clients who cannot phone during opening hours can take a published slot for a standard service.

tasks.altitude: Standard cuts and colours no longer arrive as a call. She still agrees every appointment that is not on the service list, and she can refuse a time.

reach.task: Keep the shared list of services, prices and durations the page may offer
reach.learn: A duration that is too short fills her day with appointments she cannot finish.

evidence.claim: A salon agenda product offers online booking around the clock from the salon's own site, with automatic reminders, payments and a financial overview.
The transparency duty cited in the digest applies when a chatbot takes bookings. This page offers stored services and free slots and does not chat.
In the Netherlands a works council is required from 50 staff, and consent for a booking system arises when that council exists. Other countries set their own staff-consultation rules.
Publishing durations and bookable hours is what removes the call for a standard service. How large that share is in one salon is not measured here.

assumptions: Focal boundary: the hairdresser taking, agreeing and writing appointments, and sending the reminder. Client time on the page is customer labour and is not her saving. A receptionist who takes the phones today is not in these steps.
Test the agenda's own booking page before any custom code. Time the agenda spends sending a reminder is system runtime, not her labour.

Structured offer, producer the hairdresser and the supervisor, capture in the incremental hours: service id, duration minutes, stylist id, bookable start, bookable end. A service with no duration is not offered, and s1 to s4 are not shorter for it.

Structured booking, producer the client on the page for a standard service: client name, phone, service id, start. That typing is the customer incremental hours. On a phone or chat booking the hairdresser types the same fields in s4, and that time stays inside s4.
s5 sends only when the stored booking has phone, service name and start. It restates those fields and does not offer a new time. Missing phone: no reminder is sent and she is not given a chase list.
s1 and s3 are shorter only because some requests never reach her. A call that still happens takes the same time as today. She does not listen faster, and she does not agree a time faster.
s2 is shorter only because she looks up a slot for the calls that remain. s4 is shorter only because the page writes the standard booking and she types the ones she agreed by phone or chat.
If reminders already go out without her, s5's saving does not apply. The low end of the range is that week.
unknowns: What share of this salon's requests name a service that already has a duration.
Whether a reminder is already sent without her.
Whether a works council or another staff body must consent to the booking page.
research_questions: Which services have a duration the supervisor will allow the page to sell?
What does she do today with a request that names no service?

already_counted.description: Phone and chat bookings she still hears, looks up, agrees and types.

incremental.description: Keep her bookable hours and the durations of services only she performs, and fix a clash the page allowed.
The client types name, phone, service and start for a standard appointment.
The supervisor keeps the shared service names, prices and durations the page may offer.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A week where only repeat cuts and blow-dries use the page, first visits and colour corrections stay on the phone at full length, and she still maintains durations. If reminders already send, the low end drops the reminder.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Update client records with services, products, formulas and fees.

steps.what: Open this client's card from the booking
Read the formula and the past services
Note the beauty services provided at this visit
Ring the products and the fee on the till
Copy those till lines onto the client card
Type the colour formula and any reaction
Type the preference the client just stated

tasks.design: The {OTHER} till posts each product and fee she has just rung onto the {OTHER} client card, and the card opens from the client id on today's booking. She still reads the old formula, and she still types the new formula, any reaction and the preference she heard. A product with no till line, or a booking with no client id, she writes or searches as she does today.
tasks.previous_blocker: Products and the fee were rung on the till and typed again onto the card, and the card was found by searching a box or a list.
tasks.enabler_now: The till can post a line it already holds onto the card, and the booking's client id can open that card.
tasks.still_hard: The formula and a reaction are her words, and a reaction is health data that needs a consent already on file.
tasks.human_edge: She decides the formula, and she decides whether a reaction belongs on the card.
tasks.altitude: She no longer copies products and fees, and the card opens from the booking. She still rings the till, and she still decides what is written about the colour.

reach.task: Read the reaction note before a skin treatment on the same client
reach.learn: The note is there only when the hairdresser typed it and a signed intake already covers it.

evidence.claim: A salon client card stores treatment and purchase history, appointment and treatment notes, intake forms and signed forms.
Notes on skin conditions, allergies or dye reactions are health data, and outside a care contract that usually means explicit consent.
The Dutch rule cited in the digest requires the business to keep its administration, bills and receipts for seven years. Till lines are that kind of record. Other countries set their own period.

assumptions: Focal boundary: the hairdresser finding the card before the visit and updating it after. The client paying is not a separate step; ringing the products and the fee is s4 and stays at full time.
Test a native post from till to card before custom code. The post itself is system runtime.

Till fields, producer the hairdresser in s4, capture counted there at full remaining time: product id, quantity, fee. s5 copies only those lines. A product with no till line is typed by her on the card and is outside the copy. A later change to a till line replaces the card lines; she does not edit the fee on the card.
The signed version for the copy is the till lines rung for this visit. s4 is that act. A copy made from other numbers is void.

Client id, producer the stored booking from scheduling, not this task. s1 only opens the card for that id and she still checks the name. Missing client id: she searches, and the s1 saving does not apply. This task does not count the time that created the client id.
s2 reads the formula stored at an earlier visit. She does not read this visit's formula before s6 types it. Reading and typing stay at full time. Nothing drafts them.
A reaction is stored in s6 only when a signed intake already records consent. No intake: she does not put the reaction on the shared card. Preference text in s7 is what the client said, typed by her.
unknowns: Whether this till already posts product and fee onto the card.
Whether intake forms are signed before a reaction is written.
How long this country requires the till records to be kept.
research_questions: Which card fields does the salon treat as health data?
Who rings the till when she is still with the client?

already_counted.description: Opening and reading the card, noting the visit, ringing the till, and typing the formula and the preference.

incremental.description: Check a signed intake exists before a reaction is stored, and retype a product the till did not post.

approvals.approved_version: till lines rung for this visit, each with product id, quantity and fee

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the till already posts to the card, the only new saving is opening the card from the booking, and a missed client id removes that too. Formula, preference and ringing stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Look at patrons' hair and recommend a treatment or style.

steps.what: Look at patrons' hair and physical features
Ask the patron what she wants changed
Determine the beauty treatment from that look
Recommend a treatment or suggest hair styles
Write the treatment the patron accepted

tasks.design: She looks at the patron's hair and other features, asks what should change, and recommends the treatment in her own words. Nothing proposes a style and nothing stores a scalp condition. The note of the treatment the patron accepted is still hers, on {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The treatment depends on the hair in the chair and on what the patron says she wants.
tasks.enabler_now: The booking page and the client card do not change this conversation. No tool is added.
tasks.still_hard: A poor recommendation shows on the hair and can irritate the scalp.
tasks.human_edge: She sees the hair, hears the wish, and is accountable for the treatment she recommends.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. The week is still the conversation in the chair, and she still decides the treatment.

reach.task: Recommend a cut from the same look and the same conversation
reach.learn: The recommendation is said to the patron. It is not taken from a card or a picture.

evidence.claim: Looking at the hair and recommending a treatment stays with the stylist. No product in this digest assesses hair or proposes the treatment.
A note of a skin condition, allergy or dye reaction is health data and usually needs explicit consent. This design does not write that note.

assumptions: Focal boundary: the hairdresser in the chair. No step is shorter. Looking, asking, determining and recommending are unchanged, so each stays at full remaining time.
s5 is her note of the treatment name the patron accepted. It is not a formula, a mark or a scalp score. Nothing photographs the hair.
A scalp condition she happens to see is not written here. If she later types it on the client card, the records task's consent rule applies.
No tool is added, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether this salon expects a written treatment note after every recommendation.
research_questions: Which recommendations does she already write down, and where?

already_counted.description: The look, the question, the choice, the recommendation and the short note.

incremental.description: No tool is added, so there is no upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No step is shorter. Looking, asking, determining and recommending stay as they are, and no tool is added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop new styles and techniques by trying them.

steps.what: Study techniques she might develop next
Try new styles on a practice head
Judge whether those techniques hold
Write the styles and techniques she will keep

tasks.design: She studies a technique, tries the style on a head, and judges whether it holds. The notes on {DOCS} are the steps she decided to keep, written by her. Nothing drafts a style.
tasks.previous_blocker: A new technique is learned by doing it. A written draft does not show whether it holds on hair.
tasks.enabler_now: A note can hold the steps after she has tried them. The trying and the judgement are unchanged, and no tool is added.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a technique holds depends on the hair in front of her.
tasks.human_edge: She invents the style and judges the result on a real head.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. New styles still come from trying them, and she still decides which ones to keep.

reach.task: Match makeup to a style the hairdresser has decided to keep
reach.learn: The written steps are what she kept after a trial, not a draft she has not tried.

evidence.claim: Developing a style is practice and a judgement on the result. Reading about techniques stays with her, and a draft does not replace the trial.

assumptions: Focal boundary: the hairdresser studying, trying, judging and writing a technique. No step is shorter. The design does not change the reading, the trial or the judgement.
s4 records only a technique she has already judged in s3. Nothing proposes the style.
No tool is added, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether practice on a head is part of her paid hours or her own time.
research_questions: Where does she keep a technique she has decided to repeat?

already_counted.description: Studying, trying, judging and writing the techniques she keeps.

incremental.description: No tool is added, so there is no upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No step is shorter. Studying, trying, judging and writing stay as they are, and no tool is added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still at the chair. Standard appointments land on the agenda without a call, and the card shows the till's products and fee. She still recommends the treatment and still invents styles.
skills_to_grow: Check a published service has a duration she can finish before the page offers it.
Check a reaction note is stored only when the signed intake covers it, and that the card's fee matches the till.
role.ambitious_version: Every standard cut and colour is a slot the client took, and every card opens on the formula she typed last time with the products and fee already posted from the till.
